reading: Tech stocks in the US and Asia dropped sharply after the US midterms raised fears that artificial intelligence (AI) development could slow.
Democrats across the US campaigned to limit the growth of AI and data centres, the facilities that help power the technology.
Democrats won control of both houses of Congress, the Senate and the House of Representatives.
In Texas, Gina Hinojosa, who won the race for governor, had promised to put new data centre construction on hold.
The Nasdaq Composite, an index that tracks a group of stocks, closed more than 5.5% lower.
In Japan, the Nikkei 225 was down 6% in early trading as shares in chip companies Kioxia and Tokyo Electron lost value.
In Seoul, the sell-off pushed the Kospi index down more than 8.5%, leading to a brief pause in trading to limit panic selling.
Investors were already questioning whether the large sums going into AI would pay off.
Investment strategist Charu Chanana said closer checks on data centre plans could delay projects and raise costs.
Chanana pointed to the effects of data centres on the environment and on electricity bills as issues that could face closer review.
OpenAI co-founder Greg Brockman said more work was needed to win support from local communities.
